newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan buys second Nov jet fuel cargo in tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys second Nov jet fuel cargo in tender.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought its second 32,000-tonne jet fuel cargo in its tender for November, a CPC source said on Wednesday.
This cargo was bought around the same price as the first cargo at $246.95 per tonne, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung or Shen Ao, the source said.

Trade sources said the seller of the second cargo, which is for mid-November delivery, could be the Kuwaiti-based International Petroleum Group (IPG). The first cargo for end-October/early November delivery was sold by BB Energy.
The CPC source said it is now normal for Taiwan to buy one to two cargoes of jet fuel a month and the purchase of the second cargo was not directly linked to recent problems at the Taoyuan refinery.

The refinery was shut on September 15 and production was reduced to 34 percent of capacity. The affected topping unit which has a 100,000-barrel-per-day capacity resumed operations at 74 percent on October 4.
"We bought the second cargo because we have storage space in November," the source said.
CPC also bought two jet fuel cargoes in its last tender for October 1-31 at $244.80 and $247.82 per tonne, c-and-f.
